description: This line plot illustrates how the “Shared Experts for Two Samples” metric evolves as a function of “Sample Token Count” across six different task categories: Intent, Summary, Law, Translation, Code, and Math. The x-axis, labeled “Sample Token Count,” is plotted on a logarithmic scale with tick labels representing powers of two, ranging from 2⁹ to 2²⁰. The y-axis, labeled “Shared Experts for Two Samples,” ranges from 2.0 to 6.0 on a linear scale. The orange line, representing Intent, begins near 4.0 at 2⁹ and rises to approximately 5.8 at 2²⁰. The blue line, for Summary, starts at approximately 2.0 at 2⁹, rises sharply to about 5.3 at 2¹³, then plateaus near 5.5 before slightly declining to around 5.3 at 2²⁰. The yellow line, for Law, starts near 3.8 at 2⁹, rises to about 5.7 at 2¹⁴, then fluctuates slightly before converging with the other lines near 6.0 at 2²⁰. The purple line, for Translation, begins at approximately 5.2 at 2⁹, rises to about 5.9 at 2¹³, then increases further to nearly 6.0 at 2²⁰. The gray line, for Code, starts at approximately 2.0 at 2⁹ and rises sharply to nearly 6.0 at 2¹⁶ before plateauing. The green line, for Math, begins near 3.9 at 2⁹, rises to approximately 5.5 at 2¹³, then increases to nearly 6.0 at 2²⁰. All lines show an overall increasing trend with the sample token count, with the gray line (Code) exhibiting the most dramatic initial rise before leveling off.
